While I’m neutral on this, let me play devil’s advocate:

By having anonymous comments (outside of a fully anonymous subverse), you put the named comments at a disadvantage. It would encourage users who care about their fake internet points to only post popular opinions under their name and tick the anonymous box for everything else. Essentially the anonymous option means “protect me from the consequences of this comment”.

Anonymity appeals to some — those people already post on anonymous boards. Pseudonymity appeals to some — that’s why Reddit is so big, and that’s why you’re on Voat. I think the anonymous subverse is a pretty neat feature for Voat to cater to both crowds, but allowing the two types of comments to mix will create an uneven playing field that’s not conducive to quality discussion.

And yes, throwaways already provide some form of anonymity, and throwaways are inconvenient. In my experience, it’s the users who care most about their points — the power users, the mods, the reddit pseudo-celebrities — that think it’s “necessary” to use throwaways to post their unpopular opinions. Average Joe posts his opinions and wears his upvotes and downvotes proudly, because his opinion matters more than his fake internet points.

What about people who are too afraid to post something because they're worried about of reputation being hurt? Making it inconvenient to make throwaways makes people self-censor, this way people would at the very least be expressing themselves, instead of saying something conforming that they don't mean on their main. There is obviously some demand for anonymous posting, as seen on reddit with throwaway accounts, so it's not like people aren't doing it already, this way it just makes it more convenient, and there would be no username waste.

What about people who are too afraid to post something because they're worried about of reputation being hurt?

Then they care more about their “reputation” (fake internet points) than they believe in what they’re posting, and in my opinion there is no need to make it more convenient for them to protect their reputation over someone who doesn’t shy away from posting what they believe in.

This is the problem as I see it: you^1 want “anonymity” and fake internet points at the same time. In reality you want pseudonymity when it is convenient to you (when you express a popular opinion and expect to gain upvotes and name recognition), and anonymity when it is convenient to you (when you express an unpopular opinion and expect to receive downvotes).

I don’t use anonymous boards (e.g. the various *chans), but I find them appealing because they don’t cater to people who care about fake internet points. Your posts and comments are judged for their content and nothing else. If an opinion that you sincerely hold gets downvoted or shit on, so be it! It says more about the people you are interacting with (that they downvote to disagree with you), than it says anything about the value of your opinion. Own it!

^1 by “you” I don’t mean you personally, I realised this comment may have come across more aggressive than I meant after clicking save :)
